thesis: Linde's +10% 60-day move follows confirmed Q3 2026 results (Oct 29): record sales of $9.4B (+9%), record adjusted EPS of $4.59 (+9%), Q4 adjusted EPS guidance of $4.40-$4.50 (+5-7%), full-year adjusted EPS of $17.82-$17.92, and an $11B project backlog. The strongest counter-evidence is that GAAP net income fell 12% (diluted EPS -11%) and the Q4 guide implies slower growth; even so, the GAAP decline mainly reflects a one-time $425M cost-reduction charge and a higher tax rate rather than operating weakness, and the Q4 guide still calls for year-over-year growth on a record backlog, so the read holds. This suggests disclosed fundamentals continue to support holding. The unresolved dispute over sanctioned Russian contracts and the injunction blocking sale of Russian assets has no scheduled ruling, hearing or deadline in ~90 days (narrative only). No restatement, auditor change or indictment found; board changes (CEO Lamba became chairman Feb 2026, COO named Oct 2025) were routine succession >90 days ago, and the Linde India CFO resignation (Dec 2025) is a subsidiary matter outside the window. risk_flags are empty and no binary catalyst falls before the next review.
invalidation: Q4 2026 adjusted EPS below the $4.40-$4.50 guide, a cut to full-year guidance or backlog, or further restructuring charges signaling operational weakness.

thesis: Southern Co's +12.3% 60-day gain follows a confirmed, company-disclosed catalyst: Q3 2026 adjusted EPS of $1.94 beat estimates and full-year adjusted EPS guidance was raised to $4.70, with management citing ~21 GW of large-load contracts and data-center usage up 59%. However, on Nov 12, 2026 the company priced a $1.75B offering of 2026 Series A Equity Units (reference price $92.47, threshold appreciation price $115.58) that commit holders to buy common stock by 2029 — a pending equity-linked raise within the last ~90 days, so dilution_risk applies and the rubric caps conviction at low regardless of the earnings read. A Fulton County Superior Court challenge by environmental and faith groups to the PSC's certification of ~10,000 MW of new Georgia Power generation has no ruling or hearing date found, so it is not flagged. No restatement, for-cause auditor change or executive indictment in the last 3 years (the Kemper-era SEC probe closed without enforcement; related suits settled 2021-2022). The guidance raise suggests a positive fundamental trend, but the dilution flag decides the rating.
invalidation: A cut or walk-back of the raised 2026 EPS guidance, an adverse Fulton County ruling vacating the PSC certification, or further equity/ATM issuance materially beyond the November equity units.
sources: Southern Company Q3 2026 earnings release (via Finviz): https://finviz.com/news/416808/southern-company-reports-third-quarter-2026-earnings

thesis: McDonald's +16.9% 60-day gain is anchored to its confirmed Q3 2026 report (Nov 4): adjusted EPS of $3.57 beat the $3.38 consensus, but revenue of $7.16B missed and U.S. comparable sales fell 0.2% (the first U.S. decline after five quarters of growth), with coverage noting refranchising gains flattered the beat. Much of the subsequent rally is tied to a value-bundle test across ~1,900 U.S. restaurants and a national value rollout still pending for early 2027. The evidence is mixed — a confirmed EPS beat offset by weak U.S. traffic and a not-yet-delivered catalyst — which meets the rubric's low criterion. An October 2026 consumer antitrust class action over the AI pricing tool and other suits are open with no scheduled ruling, hearing or trial in ~90 days; Jax Foods v. McDonald's (M.D. Fla.) has discovery closing Jan 29, 2027 and trial in August 2027, a procedural deadline rather than a ruling or hearing, so not flagged. The settled SEC action over former CEO Easterbrook (early 2023) is outside the 3-year window and not a restatement or indictment.
invalidation: Another quarter of negative U.S. comparable sales, the early-2027 national value rollout being delayed or failing to lift traffic, or an adverse development in the AI-pricing antitrust litigation.
sources: AP via Hawaii News Now (AI pricing lawsuit): https://www.hawaiinewsnow.com/2026/10/08/mcdonalds-sued-over-ai-tool-that-recommends-prices-us-franchisees/
Justia docket (Jax Foods LLC v. McDonald's): https://dockets.justia.com/docket/florida/flmdce/3:2026cv01396/460570

thesis: Home Depot's +18.0% 60-day gain comes with a confirmed Q3 FY2026 report (Nov 17): sales +4.9% to $43.4B, comparable sales +2.2%, adjusted diluted EPS $3.86 vs $3.74 a year earlier. The strongest counter-evidence is that the company trimmed its FY2026 outlook the same day (adjusted EPS growth ~2% from $14.69) and adjusted operating margin contracted; this is listed but not resolved, since the trim suggests comp improvement has not yet reached earnings. A CEO change took effect Nov 23 (CFO Richard McPhail succeeds Ted Decker, who stays as chair after a medical leave; Jordan Broggi becomes CFO); the 8-K frames it as succession planning with nothing tying it to execution problems, so leadership_turnover is not flagged, though it is an execution watch item. Only consumer/privacy class actions (shelf pricing, license-plate cameras, data sale, TCPA) and a plaintiff-firm securities 'investigation' were found, with no scheduled ruling, hearing or trial in ~90 days; no restatement, auditor change or indictment in the last 3 years. A real, company-specific catalyst with an unresolved guidance trim fits medium.
invalidation: Negative comparable sales or a further guidance cut in the next report, or signs the leadership transition is linked to operational problems (e.g. further unplanned C-suite exits).
sources: Home Depot Q3 FY2026 earnings release, SEC 8-K Ex. 99.1: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000354950/000035495026000184/hd_exhibit991x11012026.htm
Home Depot leadership announcement, SEC 8-K Ex. 99.1: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000354950/000035495026000182/exhibit991november2026.htm

thesis: Costco's +19% 60-day move rests on confirmed, company-disclosed events: fiscal Q4 2026 total comps +9.4% (traffic +3.3%, digital +19.5%), October comps +11.1%, and on November 10 a $30 special dividend ($13.3B, payable Dec 4 to holders of record today) plus a new $4B buyback. The strongest counter-evidence is that headline numbers are inflated — gasoline inflation added ~3.9 points to October comps, Q4 EPS included a one-time $0.15 IEEPA tariff-refund benefit, and today's ex-dividend drop is mechanical — but even with those stripped out the company's own table shows comps ex-gas/FX of ~6.7% (7.2% U.S.) with positive traffic, so the read holds. This suggests the underlying business supports holding. The consumer tariff-refund class action (N.D. Ill.) and Costco's stayed CIT suit have no scheduled ruling/hearing/trial; the Salisbury Ninth Circuit appeal has only an appellant opening-brief deadline (Dec 1), not a ruling or compliance deadline, so not flagged. No restatement, for-cause auditor change, indictment, equity raise, liquidity issue or C-suite departure found, and no binary catalyst before the next review (fiscal Q1 earnings later in December).
invalidation: Monthly comps ex-gas/FX turning flat or negative, falling traffic, or a court ruling forcing tariff-refund pass-through material to earnings.
sources: Costco Q4 FY2026 press release via Finviz: https://finviz.com/news/395411/costco-wholesale-corporation-reports-fourth-quarter-and-fiscal-year-2026-operating-results

thesis: P&G sits at its 52-week high after a +16.0% 60-day move. The company-disclosed backdrop is its Oct 22 FY2027 Q1 report: organic sales +4%, but diluted EPS only +1% to $1.97, gross margin down 160 bps, and EPS-growth guidance held at 1%-5%. Trefis attributes the rally largely to multiple expansion (P/E ~24.7 vs 20.2 a year ago) rather than earnings growth, framing the move as sentiment/valuation-driven rather than a disclosed fundamental change, which meets the rubric's low criterion. Consumer false-advertising class actions (phenylephrine revived by the Second Circuit; Metamucil; ZzzQuil; Kid's Crest) are proceeding with no scheduled ruling, hearing or trial in ~90 days; the Texas AG fluoride probe was resolved by agreed order. No restatement, for-cause auditor change or indictment in the last 3 years; CEO Jejurikar's succession and chair appointment were planned internal moves; no dilution (Q1 included $1.3B of buybacks).
invalidation: Organic sales growth slowing below the low end of guidance, a cut to FY2027 EPS guidance, or gross-margin compression large enough to break the 1%-5% EPS-growth range.
sources: P&G FY2027 Q1 results press release: https://us.pg.com/newsroom/news-releases/PG-Announces-Fiscal-Year-2027-First-Quarter-Results/

thesis: Lilly's +15.3% 60-day move is anchored by confirmed Q3 2026 results (Oct 29): revenue +39% to $24.4B on Mounjaro and Zepbound, with the 2026 revenue guidance midpoint raised by $5.5B to $91-92B; recent FDA approvals (including Mounjaro's cardiovascular indication) and ObesityWeek data add support. The counter-evidence weighed is valuation skepticism (e.g. an earlier HSBC downgrade to reduce), which is analyst opinion and does not outweigh the disclosed guidance raise. Conviction stays medium because the driver of today's ~3.3% gain wasn't identified and several legal matters have unresolved next steps without confirmed dates: GLP-1 GI-injury MDL 3094 (~3,848 cases; Rule 702 expert ruling outcome unconfirmed), the Streck whistleblower case headed to a jury with no trial date, and Lilly's Seventh Circuit dispute with FDA over retatrutide regulation (no argument scheduled). None has a specific scheduled event within ~90 days, so active_litigation is not flagged, but the pending expert ruling is an unresolved binary item. No restatement, auditor change, indictment, dilution, liquidity issue or C-suite departure found; this suggests fundamentals still support holding.
invalidation: A cut to 2026 revenue guidance or slowing Mounjaro/Zepbound growth, an MDL 3094 expert ruling admitting plaintiffs' causation experts, or a setback to the retatrutide filing timeline (BLA planned Q1 2027).
sources: U.S. District Court E.D. Pa. MDL 3094 order: https://www.paed.uscourts.gov/sites/paed/files/mdl-orders/24md3094_cm-ord_29.pdf
Justia Dockets (Eli Lilly v. Kennedy, 7th Cir.): https://dockets.justia.com/docket/circuit-courts/ca7/26-1301

thesis: Visa's +11.4% 60-day move follows confirmed fiscal Q4 2026 results (Oct 27): net revenue $12.1B (+13%), non-GAAP EPS $3.48 (+17%), cross-border volume +14%, and a 16% dividend increase to $0.78. The counter-evidence is legal: after a November 16, 2026 fairness hearing, Judge Cogan has not yet ruled on final approval of the $38B merchant interchange settlement (Walmart and NRF object; rejection could send the case to trial in 2027), and the DOJ debit monopolization suit (No. 24-cv-7214, S.D.N.Y.) survived dismissal with trial expected late 2027-2028 and no scheduled step within ~90 days. Because the final-approval ruling has no specific scheduled date, active_litigation is not flagged, but it is an unresolved binary catalyst that could land before the next review, capping conviction at medium despite strong results; the June preliminary approval (calling the deal fair, reasonable and adequate) suggests the ruling is not obviously adverse. No restatement, auditor change or indictment found; the CEO's November share sale appears routine; no dilution, liquidity or leadership-turnover issues.
invalidation: Judge Cogan rejecting the $38B interchange settlement, an adverse development in the DOJ debit case, or payments/cross-border volume growth slowing well below fiscal Q4 rates.

thesis: SKHY's -35.1% 60-day decline, new 52-week low on Nov 20 and -9.9% drop today come despite a confirmed record Q3 2026 (revenue 104.6T won, operating profit 83.3T won, ~80% margin), a 14T won dividend and 20T won buyback, and long-term agreements covering more than half of 2027-2028 capacity. Coverage attributes the selloff to memory/AI-semiconductor sector moves — doubts about the durability of AI-memory pricing, Chinese competition and capacity expansion, and a broad Nov 5 semiconductor rout alongside MU, NVDA and AMD — a sector/sentiment-driven move rather than a disclosed company deterioration, which meets the rubric's low criterion. The October report of delayed HBM4 equipment orders is the closest company-specific negative but is unconfirmed as a fundamental change; the record results are the strongest counter-evidence and suggest the price action does not reflect a confirmed earnings break. The USITC Section 337 patent investigation (337-TA-1492, MonolithIC 3D) and related suits have no scheduled ruling or hearing found within ~90 days; a former employee was indicted in May 2025 for allegedly leaking packaging technology to a Huawei-linked firm (a governance_history item within 3 years); the July 2026 ADR offering falls outside the ~90-day dilution window. With a falling-knife sector backdrop and no company-specific positive driving price, the read is avoid at low conviction.
invalidation: Stabilization of the memory/AI-semiconductor complex together with confirmed HBM4 volume ramp and pricing in the Q4 report, or a sustained recovery off the Nov 20 low on company-specific news.

thesis: Apple trades near its 52-week high after confirmed fiscal Q4 2026 results: revenue of $114.5B (+12%) beat estimates, with continued large buybacks ($85.8B in FY2026). Counter-points include slowing China sales growth, management-flagged memory-cost pressure and a post-report dip. Under the rubric the deciding factor is litigation: the Supreme Court has set oral argument for January 11, 2027 in Apple v. Epic Games (No. 25-1311) on the App Store contempt order, with Apple's reply brief due December 14 — both inside ~90 days, so active_litigation is flagged and conviction is capped at low regardless of the earnings beat. The DOJ antitrust case has no trial date (reported 2027+, settlement talks) and is narrative only. The Ternus CEO succession (Sept 1, 2026) was planned, board-approved and >90 days ago, so it is not leadership_turnover; the $7.5B November note sale is debt, not dilution; no restatement, for-cause auditor change or executive indictment found. This suggests fundamentals still support holding, but the scheduled Supreme Court event keeps conviction low.
invalidation: A Supreme Court ruling or remand that widens restrictions on commissions for outside purchases, or disclosed iPhone/Services weakness or memory-cost margin pressure that erases fiscal Q4 growth.

thesis: No company-specific news was found for today's ~5.6% drop; November weakness has been attributed to post-midterm regulation worries, a broad AI/tech selloff, hedge-fund profit-taking (Nomura's McElligott), and caution around Starship tests. The clearest disclosed structural risk is the IPO lockup expiry on Dec 8, about two weeks away, when tradable float is set to rise sharply (reports cite roughly 40% of shares), which suggests near-term supply pressure. Counter-evidence includes SpaceX catching Starship's upper stage on Nov 14 and Mizuho keeping an Outperform through an earlier unlock during which shares rose; these are listed but do not outweigh the scheduled supply event, so the read stays avoid without high confidence. The SEC's case against Elon Musk personally over his Twitter-stake disclosure is unresolved (sources conflict on settlement; no scheduled date within ~90 days found); investor disputes in Delaware/Texas and an advocacy group's SEC complaint about its financials carry no confirmed finding; no restatement, auditor change or indictment was found.
invalidation: Shares absorb the Dec 8 unlock without further weakness and hold above the ~$135 IPO price, or a company-disclosed fundamental positive (results or a major contract) outweighs the supply overhang.
sources: Bloomberg Law (SpaceX financials flagged to SEC): https://news.bloomberglaw.com/esg/spacex-financials-flagged-as-concern-to-sec-by-advocacy-group

thesis: Today's +14.1% move on 17.9x volume with an unusually narrow range matches a signed deal: Sanofi announced on 2026-11-24 an agreement to acquire Insmed for $175 per share in cash (~$41.0B equity value, ~46% premium to the unaffected 11/18 close), expected to close in 1H27 subject to regulatory approval, the Insmed shareholder vote and customary conditions. This is a confirmed, company-disclosed event that caps upside at roughly 2.8% ($170.18 vs $175) while carrying months of deal-break risk. The strongest counter-evidence is a possible competing bid (earlier Bloomberg-sourced reporting suggested other bidders could emerge), but even with that possibility a topping bid is speculation rather than a disclosed event, so the setup suggests merger-arbitrage rather than a directional long. Litigation/governance checks found only plaintiff-firm 'investigation' solicitations tied to the Dec 2025 BiRCh trial failure, with no filed complaint or scheduled hearing in the next ~90 days; no restatement, auditor change or indictment was found. A CFO departure was reported (company said unrelated to any accounting disagreement; date not confirmed this run). The vote/regulatory approvals fall after the next review window and do not reverse this read.
invalidation: A competing bid or raised Sanofi offer that reopens meaningful upside above the current price, or deal termination/blocking (forcing a re-evaluation of standalone fundamentals).

thesis: The +19.9% move on 5.5x volume coincides with Amentum's fiscal Q4/FY2026 results (8-K dated 11/23/2026, call 11/24): FY revenue $13.8B, adjusted EBITDA $1,132M (+3%), adjusted diluted EPS $2.51, 50 bps margin expansion, $17B of awards, $48.3B backlog, and a first-ever $500M share repurchase authorization. This suggests the market rewarded the margin and capital-return story, but this run could not locate the FY2027 guidance figures or post-report coverage explaining the move, so multiple contributing factors are listed without one clearly resolved as dominant. Counter-evidence remains open: Q4 revenue fell 8% y/y (largely an extra week in the prior-year quarter) and earlier disclosures flagged a NASA insourcing headwind of ~3% of FY27 revenue, which this thesis does not resolve. Inherited/ongoing False Claims Act whistleblower suits (Air Force subcontract-stacking; a former AECOM unit's Afghanistan contract) and bid protests exist, but no scheduled ruling, hearing or trial within ~90 days was found; no restatement, auditor change or indictment in the last 3 years; no dilution (buyback, not a raise), liquidity concern, or C-suite turnover.
invalidation: FY27 guidance or call commentary showing NASA insourcing/program-exit headwinds deepening into a larger revenue decline, the stock fully giving back the post-earnings gap, or an adverse scheduled development in the FCA litigation.

thesis: The two-day move (+30% on 11/23, +15.7% today to a new 52-week high on 4.8x volume) follows Kymera's 11/23/2026 release of positive topline Phase 2b BROADEN2 results for KT-621, its oral STAT6 degrader, in moderate-to-severe atopic dermatitis: the trial met its primary EASI endpoint at Week 16 with statistically significant improvement vs placebo across all dose cohorts (mid-dose ~45% placebo-adjusted mean EASI reduction, ~40% placebo-adjusted EASI-75) and was well tolerated. This is a confirmed, company-disclosed catalyst and suggests a credible oral challenger in a Dupixent-dominated market. The main counter-evidence is not resolved: biotechs commonly raise equity right after data and none was found yet (the last raise, Dec 2025, falls outside the 90-day window), Phase 3 doesn't start until mid-2027, and the stock has already rerated ~50% in two days. Plaintiff-firm 'investigations' (Purcell & Lefkowitz, Kuehn Law) into alleged director fiduciary breaches were announced May–July 2026 with no filed suit or scheduled step found; no restatement, auditor change, indictment, or recent C-suite turnover was found.
invalidation: An equity or convertible offering announced on the back of the data, full data showing weaker durability or safety than the topline, or the shares giving back most of the two-day post-data gain.
